resources.title: Istanbulkart
resources.description: The must-have reloadable transit card. Works on metro, tram, bus, ferry and funicular. Tap-to-pay everywhere.
resources.tip: Buy at any metro station kiosk for ₺70 (card deposit). Reload at machines or the app. Saves ~35% vs cash fares.

resources.title: Metro & Tram
resources.description: M2 connects Taksim to the airport (Gayrettepe). T1 tram runs Kabataş–Eminönü–Bağcılar. M4 links Kadıköy to Sabiha Gökçen airport.
resources.tip: Service runs 06:00–midnight. During rush hour (08–10, 17–19) expect full carriages on M2.

resources.title: Ferry (Şehir Hatları)
resources.description: Scenic and cheap Bosphorus crossings. Key routes: Eminönü ↔ Kadıköy, Beşiktaş ↔ Kadıköy, Kabataş ↔ Üsküdar.
resources.tip: Ferries run every 15–30 min during daytime. The upper deck is worth it for the views. Istanbulkart accepted.

resources.title: Taxi & Rideshare
resources.description: Yellow taxis (taksi) are abundant. Apps: BiTaksi (official taxi app) and Uber both work in Istanbul.
resources.tip: Always confirm the meter is running. Uber is often slightly cheaper and avoids negotiation. Typical city ride: ₺150–400.

resources.title: Dolmuş
resources.description: Shared minibuses running fixed routes. Cash only, extremely cheap. Tell the driver your stop and pay when you get off.
resources.tip: No apps for dolmuş — learn the route from locals. Great for short trips where metro doesn't reach.

resources.title: Funicular & Cable Car
resources.description: F1 funicular (Kabataş ↔ Taksim), F2 (Taksim ↔ İstiklal). Teleferik cable cars in Eyüp and Maçka park.
resources.tip: Istanbulkart works. F2 is the famous nostalgic tram on İstiklal Caddesi — lovely but slow.

resources.title: Google Maps
resources.description: Best overall navigation. Accurately routes metro, tram, ferry, and bus with real-time departures.
resources.tip: Download the Istanbul offline map before you arrive. Works great in tunnels once cached.

resources.title: Moovit
resources.description: Transit-focused directions with live departures and step-by-step guidance for Istanbul's full public transport network.

resources.title: BiTaksi
resources.description: Official Istanbul taxi app. Connects you to licensed yellow taxis with upfront pricing and driver tracking.

resources.title: Getir & Yemeksepeti
resources.description: Getir for ultra-fast grocery/convenience delivery (10–30 min). Yemeksepeti for restaurant food delivery.
resources.tip: Getir is genuinely 10 minutes. Both apps have English interfaces and work with foreign cards.

resources.title: Istanbul Kart App
resources.description: Check your Istanbulkart balance, view trip history, and reload your card without finding a kiosk.

resources.title: Trendyol
resources.description: Turkey's largest e-commerce app. Same-day delivery for most items in Istanbul. Also has Trendyol Go for food.
resources.tip: Significantly cheaper than Amazon equivalent for electronics, home goods, and clothing.

resources.title: Sahibinden.com
resources.description: Turkey's main real estate platform. Listings for both long-term rentals and sales across all neighbourhoods. The default starting point.
resources.tip: Filter by 'Kiralık' (for rent) and your target neighbourhood. Many listings are agent-only — expect a 1-month commission fee.

resources.title: Typical Rental Costs
resources.description: 1-bed in Cihangir/Beyoğlu: ₺25,000–55,000/mo. Kadıköy/Moda: ₺20,000–45,000/mo. Beşiktaş/Nişantaşı: ₺40,000–80,000/mo. Emerging areas (Eyüp, Bağcılar): ₺12,000–22,000/mo.
resources.tip: Prices rise fast. Fully-furnished flats list at a premium (20–40% above bare). Negotiate hard — most landlords expect it.

resources.title: Facebook Groups
resources.description: Best source for direct-from-landlord listings and expat sublets: search 'Istanbul Expats Housing', 'Istanbul Apartments for Rent', 'Expats in Istanbul'.
resources.tip: Post your requirements in the group — many members rent rooms or sublet short-term. Faster than agent listings.

resources.title: What to Expect
resources.description: Standard lease is 12 months. Deposit is typically 1–2 months rent. Utilities (elektrik, su, doğalgaz) are billed separately. Many buildings have an aidat (building maintenance fee).
resources.tip: Ask for the contract in English or get a translation. Always confirm if bills are included (eşyalı = furnished, faturalar dahil = bills included).

resources.title: Traps to Avoid
resources.description: Fake listings reusing photos from other properties. Agents asking for fees upfront before showing. Landlords who won't provide a formal contract (kira sözleşmesi).
resources.tip: Always verify the landlord owns the property (ask for tapu — title deed). Meet in person before paying anything. Use bank transfer, not cash, for the deposit.

resources.title: Short-Term on Arrival
resources.description: For your first weeks: Airbnb and Booking.com have strong Istanbul supply. Monthly Airbnb is often 30–40% cheaper than the nightly rate — always ask the host.
resources.tip: Neighbourhoods with high Airbnb supply: Taksim, Sultanahmet, Karaköy, Kadıköy. Avoid tourist-trap rates in Sultanahmet for long stays.

resources.title: Turkish Breakfast (Kahvaltı)
resources.description: A weekend ritual. Spread of cheeses, olives, tomatoes, cucumbers, eggs, honey, clotted cream, and börek. Normally served until early afternoon.
resources.tip: Best areas: Kadıköy, Cihangir, Van (the city known for its kahvaltı culture). Budget ₺200–400pp at a sit-down place.

resources.title: Street Food Essentials
resources.description: Simit (sesame bread ring, ₺10–15), balık ekmek (fish sandwich on Eminönü waterfront, ₺100), kestane (roasted chestnuts in winter), midye (stuffed mussels).
resources.tip: Midye — squeeze lemon on each mussel and pay per piece at the end. A great street snack at ₺10–15 each.

resources.title: Markets
resources.description: Kadıköy Çarşı: best everyday food market on the Asian side. Mısır Çarşısı (Spice Bazaar, Eminönü): spices, Turkish delight, dried fruit. Kapalıçarşı (Grand Bazaar): souvenirs and textiles.
resources.tip: For fresh produce at local prices, use the neighbourhood pazar (street market) — each area has one on a different day of the week.

resources.title: Alcohol & Rakı Culture
resources.description: Turkey produces good wine (especially Thrace and Cappadocia regions) and Efes beer. Rakı is the national spirit — anise-flavoured, diluted with water. Meyhane restaurants are the traditional setting.
resources.tip: Alcohol is only sold in licensed shops and restaurants. Supermarkets cannot sell alcohol between midnight and 06:00. Prices are high due to taxes — budget ₺200–400 for a beer in a bar.

resources.title: Coffee Culture
resources.description: Istanbul has an excellent specialty coffee scene alongside traditional Turkish coffee (türk kahvesi). Neighborhoods like Karaköy, Cihangir, and Nişantaşı have dense café clusters.
resources.tip: Turkish coffee is unfiltered — don't drink the last sip. Ordering 'az şekerli' (little sugar) or 'şekersiz' (no sugar) is respected.

resources.title: Delivery Apps
resources.description: Yemeksepeti (restaurant delivery), Getir Yemek (fast food + grocery), Trendyol Yemek (restaurant + market). All work with foreign cards and have English interfaces.
resources.tip: Delivery is fast (20–40 min average) and relatively cheap. Tipping delivery drivers is not culturally expected but appreciated.

resources.title: Kolektif House
resources.description: Istanbul's premium co-working network. Multiple locations: Maslak, Ataşehir, Bağcılar, Beşiktaş. High-speed fibre, meeting rooms, good community events.
resources.tip: Day passes available from ~₺600. Monthly memberships from ~₺4,000. Book meeting rooms via the app.

resources.title: Workinton
resources.description: Good value co-working with many Istanbul locations. More casual atmosphere than Kolektif. Strong on amenities (printing, lockers, phone booths).
resources.tip: Monthly plans from ~₺3,000. Offer short-term packages ideal for visitors staying a few weeks.

resources.title: Café Working Culture
resources.description: Istanbul cafés are generally very laptop-friendly. No pressure to leave, outlets at most tables, decent Wi-Fi. Kadıköy, Cihangir, Karaköy, and Nişantaşı have the densest options.
resources.tip: Order every 1.5–2 hours and you're welcome to stay all day. Specialty coffee spots often have faster Wi-Fi than chains.

resources.title: Internet & Connectivity
resources.description: Istanbul has excellent fibre internet infrastructure. Most apartments and cafés offer 100–500 Mbps. Get a local SIM for 4G/5G backup (Turkcell is most reliable).
resources.tip: Some services are throttled or blocked (Discord, certain VoIP). Set up a VPN before arriving — downloading from Turkey can be slow.

resources.title: Work & Visa Considerations
resources.description: Most expats work remotely on tourist visas. Turkish residence permits (ikamet) are required after 90 days. Freelancers can explore the 'digital nomad' visa option introduced in 2023.
resources.tip: Stay on top of your 90/180-day Schengen-style limit. Many expats do 'visa runs' to a nearby country. Always consult a local immigration lawyer for complex situations.

resources.title: Time Zone & Working with Europe
resources.description: Istanbul is UTC+3. 1 hour ahead of most of Europe, 8 hours ahead of US East Coast. Works well for European clients with morning Istanbul time = late night Europe.
resources.tip: Turkish public holidays differ from European ones. Check the calendar at the start of each month to avoid surprises.

resources.title: SIM Card
resources.description: Buy a Turkcell tourist SIM at the airport or any Turkcell store. 30-day unlimited data plans from ~₺500.
resources.tip: Foreign phones must be registered within 120 days or they'll be blocked on Turkish networks. Ask the store about IMEI registration.

resources.title: Currency & ATMs
resources.description: Turkish Lira (TRY). Use ATMs from major banks: Garanti, İş Bankası, Yapı Kredi. Avoid airport exchange booths.
resources.tip: Many restaurants and shops prefer cash. Always carry some TRY. Revolut and Wise work great here for card payments with interbank rates.

resources.title: Healthcare
resources.description: Private hospitals are excellent and used by expats: Acıbadem, Memorial, American Hospital. English-speaking doctors available.
resources.tip: Emergency: 112. Visits without insurance typically ₺800–2,000 for consultations. Keep your receipts for insurance reimbursement.

resources.title: Emergency Numbers
resources.description:
112 — Ambulance & Fire
155 — Police
156 — Gendarmerie
158 — Coast Guard

resources.title: VPN
resources.description: Some platforms are throttled or intermittently blocked in Turkey (Discord, some social media). A reliable VPN is recommended.
resources.tip: Mullvad and ProtonVPN work well. Set up before you arrive — download speeds from Turkey can make VPN setup slow.

resources.title: Language Tips
resources.description: Turkish is phonetic — pronunciation is consistent once you learn it. Most younger locals in expat areas speak English.
resources.tip: 'Teşekkürler' (teh-shek-kür-ler) = Thank you. 'Merhaba' = Hello. Learning a few words goes a long way with locals.
